Unlike histogram-based methods that rely on intensity distributions, Contour Spectrum focuses on the topological and geometric properties of the isosurfaces themselves, using a directed acyclic graph to track their evolution [S1, unofficial][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that Contour Spectrum focuses on topological and geometric properties of isosurfaces (unlike histogram-based methods) and uses a directed acyclic graph (DAG) to track their evolution. Source [S2] explicitly confirms that Bajaj et al. (1997) proposed measures based on the scalar field (area, volume, gradient integral) which are geometric/topological properties, and that the approach includes implementing a 'directed acyclic graph structure representing the topological behavior of isosurfaces' where separations and junctions are registered. Source [S1] contrasts this with later methods by Kindlmann and Durkin that used histograms, and notes that Contour Spectrum assimilates Surface Fitting resources. Thus, the evidence supports the distinction from histogram methods and the use of a DAG for topological tracking.
